`manifest.json`, the logo and the README candidates. No `logs/` path is in it, not even `*.log`, so a module
published through the enricher's HuggingFace publisher carries a manifest whose `logs` names files the repository
does not hold. `verify --check-logs` skips an absent log by design, so nothing reports the gap. RM338 widened what
`logs/` ships at compile, which makes the difference larger: an author who sees `log ships: …` at compile then
publishes a module without it.

**The patch.** The allowlist takes every path `manifest.logs` names, derived from the manifest the directory
carries rather than restated as a pattern (`@publisher-allowlist-derived`). A test publishes (plans the upload of)
a module with `.log`, `.jsonl` and `.png` logs and asserts each is in the plan. Not decided here: whether a log
the manifest does not name, present on disk, is uploaded; the default is no.

**Shipped.** `plan_upload` appends every path `manifest.logs` names to `UploadPlan.files`, read field by
field out of the manifest JSON by the reader the attestation check already used (now one helper,
`_manifest_document`), never a glob. The open default is decided as filed: a file under `logs/` the manifest
does not name is **not** uploaded. A named path that is absolute, contains `..`, resolves outside the module
directory through a symlink is skipped with a warning naming the reason, and the publish goes on; there was no
path-escape guard elsewhere to match, so this one checks both the spelling and the resolved path. A hidden
path is refused on the compiler's terms rather than a second rule: discovery ships a hidden `*.log` and no
other hidden kind, so the publisher does the same. A blanket hidden refusal was written first and withdrawn,
because it recreated this item's defect for a hidden `.log` the manifest names. Whatever `upload_folder`'s
default ignore list drops (`.git`, `.cache/huggingface`, read from `huggingface_hub`) is refused even as a
`.log`, since the hub would never send it. A named log
absent from disk is skipped quietly, and an absent or unreadable manifest plans no logs, as before.
`upload_module` now passes the plan itself, glob-escaped, as `upload_folder`'s allowlist rather than
`_ALLOW_PATTERNS`, so the dry run is the upload (the snapshot publisher's rule): the hub matches with `fnmatch`,
and a compiler-shipped `logs/fig[1].png` unescaped selected `logs/fig1.png` instead. Tests compile a copy of
`apoe_epsilon` with a `.log`, a nested `.jsonl` and two `.png` logs, and check the plan, the unnamed file, the
escaping and hidden spellings plus an unresolvable one (a NUL, on which `Path.resolve` raises), and what
huggingface_hub's own filter, default ignore list included, selects from the files on disk; each derivation was
mutated once to watch its test go red.

**Residuals** none

## RM353 — the module publisher diverges from what the manifest declares: provenance is never uploaded, snapshot names are not glob-escaped, and a logs-only republish overwrites a version

**Severity** medium · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-11-04 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (filed 2026-11-04 by the lead) · **Owner** enricher (`upload._declared_files`, `upload.plan_upload`, `upload._versioned_conflict`, `upload._literal_patterns`) · **Motivating case** found while building RM347 · *related* RM347

**One class: the publisher's plan and guard are not derived from what the manifest says it holds.** Three instances:

1. `provenance.json` is named with a sha256 in `manifest.provenance.file`, and no allowlist includes it, so it is
   never uploaded;
2. `publish_reference_snapshot` passes file names to the hub as glob patterns unescaped (RM347 escaped the module
   publisher's), so a name with `[` selects a different file;
3. the overwrite guard for `data/<name>/v<version>/` compares only `artifact.digest`, which excludes logs by design,
   so a second publish with changed logs replaces them without `--force`.

The fix derives the upload set from every file entry the manifest declares (artifact, logs, provenance, logo, readme),
escapes every pattern in both publishers through one helper, and widens the guard's comparison to the declared
files' hashes. Not in scope, under the existing rule: the flat `data/<name>/` path keeps stale files, since a publish
deletes only what was declared (`@a-publish-may-not-orphan-the-bytes-it-stops-describing`).

**Shipped.** One helper, `_declared_files`, reads every file the manifest declares in the module directory out
of the JSON `_manifest_document` returns: `artifact.files`, `logo`, `readme`, `provenance` (a summary carrying
`file` and `sha256`, which is why a `FileEntry` walk never saw it) and `logs`. `inputs` and `derived` are left
out, since they describe files beside the spec. `plan_upload` sends `manifest.json` plus those files when
`artifact.files` is legible, and **nothing else**: a parquet an earlier compile left in the directory, or a logo
the manifest does not name, now stays behind (the old allowlist sent both, and a stale parquet on the flat path
reads to discovery as part of the module). RM347's path guard, renamed `_declared_refusal_reason`, reads every
declared name, so a hand-edited `provenance.file` of `../x` is skipped with a warning; an attested parquet
refused or absent still raises rule 1, and an optional one absent is skipped quietly. A declared file whose
bytes on disk no longer hash to the stated sha256 refuses the plan (found in review: the guard compares
manifests, so a log appended to after the compile would otherwise pass it). With no readable manifest
or no `artifact.files` list the plan falls back to `_ALLOW_PATTERNS` on disk, as before. `_literal_patterns` is
the one escaping helper, applied to the module publisher's `allow_patterns`, both of the snapshot publisher's,
the declared retirement's `delete_patterns` (`LayoutShift.retires` is one name, never a glob) and, beyond the
two publishers the item named, `prune_repo`'s `delete_patterns`, where an unescaped listed name would delete a
file nobody was shown. The guard, `_versioned_conflict`, compares `artifact.digest` and then every declared
file's sha256; a hash that differs, or a file declared on one side only, is a `PublishCollisionError` whose
message says *the same compiled data but different declared files* and names each one. A declaration with no
legible hash is not compared. `PublishCollisionError` stays the type on `main`. One test fixture changed with
it: the RM199 retirement test passed `retires="data/old-*.parquet"`, a glob the field forbids, and now passes a
name. Tests compile copies of `apoe_epsilon` carrying a `provenance.json`, a logo, a README and a log, and check
the plan against the declared set, an undeclared stale parquet and logo, an escaping `provenance.file`, a
snapshot file `data/chr[1].parquet` beside a `data/chr1.parquet` decoy, a retirement and a prune of a `[` name,
a logs-only recompile at the same version (digest equal, refused, then sent under `force`), and a log declared
on one side only. Each derivation was mutated once to watch its tests go red: the provenance arm, the derived
plan (back to the allowlist union), the escaping helper, and the declared-hash comparison.

**Residuals** none

## RM355 — the module publisher reads one manifest three ways, so `upload --dry-run` tracebacks on every refusal

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-11-04 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (filed 2026-11-04 by the lead) · **Owner** enricher (`upload.py`, `cli.py upload`) · **Motivating
case** a 0.8 builder's report, 2026-11-04, reading the RM353 publisher · *related* RM347, RM353

**One class: one manifest, several readers and filters.** RM353 gave the plan and the guard one reader of what the
manifest declares (`_declared_files`), but three readings are still apart:

1. `upload --dry-run` calls `plan_upload` outside the `try` that the real run's `upload_module` sits in, so a
   refusal the real run reports as a message comes out of a dry run as a traceback;
2. `_module_version` opens and parses `manifest.json` itself instead of reading `_manifest_document`'s object, so
   the version and the file list come from two reads;
3. `_named_entries` keeps an entry whose `name` is `""`, which `_declared_files` drops, so the attested-parquet
   list and the declared list disagree on the same entry.

**The fix, as one rule.** One reader of the manifest document and one filter of its file entries, which every
helper calls; the dry run goes through the same refusal handling as the real run and prints the same message.

**Shipped.** One reader: `_manifest_document` returns the parsed object together with the reason there is none
(absent, unparseable, not an object), and `_module_version` is now a pure function of that pair, so the four
`version_unknown_reason` strings are unchanged. `plan_upload` reads once and builds the plan through
`_plan_from_document`; `upload_module` reads once and hands the same object to the plan and to
`_versioned_conflict`, where it used to read the file a third time. One filter: `_named_entry` keeps an
object whose `name` is a non-empty string, with its `sha256` or `None`, and `_attested_parquets`,
`_declared_files` and the plan's new refusal all read through it (`_named_entries` is gone), so the two lists
agree about an `artifact.files` entry named `""`. The plan refuses that entry, quoting it, rather than dropping
it: it is inside `artifact.digest`, so dropping it quietly would publish a digest no upload can satisfy
(`@an-absent-input-is-the-unknown-arm-and-a-malformed-one-is-the-refusal`; found in review, after a first
build that dropped it). It used to refuse too, as `attests ['']` with a hint to recompile "if the file is
missing". An optional declaration naming no file stays dropped, since it is outside the digest. `upload --dry-run` now calls `plan_upload`
inside the same `try` as the real run, so a refusal prints the same `UPLOAD FAILED: …` line and exits 1
without a traceback. The dry run still contacts nothing, so it cannot report a versioned-path collision,
which needs the published manifest; the test uses a refusal the plan raises (a declared log appended to after
the compile) and compares the dry run's stderr with the real run's. ENRICHER.md's signature block gains
`upload_module`'s `force` and both snapshot functions' keyword-only `payload`. Tests: the dry run and the real
run on one refused module (same stderr, `SystemExit` rather than the refusal), a counting test over
`io.open` on `manifest.json`, which every way of reading a file passes through (one read for a plan and one
for a publish), and an empty-name entry (absent from both lists, refused with the entry quoted). Each was
mutated once and went red: the dry run moved back outside the `try`, a second read inside the plan (through
`read_text`, then `read_bytes`), the filter without its empty-name guard, and the refusal removed.

**Residuals** none

## RM354 — the GWAS Catalog retired the legacy REST API the `gwas` pass reads, so `gwas_effects.csv` cannot be filled for a new module

**Severity** high · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-11-04 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (filed 2026-11-04 by the lead; widened to the class by the lead the same day) · **Owner** enricher (`gwas`, `net`, and every client in `test_client_exception_contract.CLIENTS`) · **Motivating case** the RM333
builder's report, 2026-11-04, recorded in `docs/probes/LANES_0_8.md` §5.5 on `build/RM333` · *related* RM239,
RM333, `@client-exception-contract`

**One class: a source retired an API surface, and the client has no finding for it.** `GwasCatalogClient` asks
`https://www.ebi.ac.uk/gwas/rest/api/singleNucleotidePolymorphisms/<rsid>/associations` (`DEFAULT_GWAS_ENDPOINT`).
That endpoint now answers HTTP 410, "This legacy GWAS Catalog REST API is no longer available", pointing at the
v2 migration guide; `/gwas/rest/api/v2/associations?rs_id=` answers 200. The 410 falls into the generic
`httpx.HTTPError` arm and becomes a plain `GwasError`, which the pass records as could-not-ask. So every rsID of
every new module reads as an outage, nothing is filled, and nothing says the source moved. RM239's posterior is
filled only on `gwas_effects.csv` rows that already exist.

**The fix, as one rule.** The client moves to the v2 endpoint (its response shape probed from the real answer
first, `@probe-the-real-file`), and a 410 from any endpoint raises a named retired-endpoint error, a `GwasError`
subclass whose message carries the URL and the source's own text, never the generic failure. A subclass makes a
caller's `except` order load-bearing, so the handler shapes are enumerated before it lands. Every other client
that maps status codes gets the same 410 arm, since retirement is a currency fact about the source, not one
lane's bug.

**What the hand-run found (2026-11-04).** The legacy path answers 410, `text/plain`, on every path
including `/studies/<accession>`. v2 answers `associations?rs_id=rs4149056` with 20 of 386 per page and a
`_links.next`; `size=1000` returns all of them. Three facts shaped the client. **The empty answer is a 200
with no `_embedded` key at all** (`page.totalElements: 0`), for a rare variant and a nonexistent rsID alike,
so the legacy guard ("no `_embedded.associations` means the shape changed") would have refused every
clinically-authored module on its first rare variant; it now raises only when the page does not say zero.
**A 404 stopped being an answer**: the only one v2's search gave was a wrong path, so `associations_for` no
longer reads it as "no associations" and `gwas` left `FOUR_OH_FOUR_IS_AN_ANSWER`. **The effect is one
composite string** (`"0.05 umol/l increase"`, `"-"` beside an odds ratio), parsed by one grammar and withheld
whole outside it. `standard_error` has no v2 field and stays null; `pmid`, accession and EFO trait are inline,
so ancestry (`/studies/<accession>/ancestries`) is the only follow and the request budget on
`hfe_hemochromatosis` fell from 382 to 190. The association ids carried over (legacy 13069 and 55421052 are
v2's too), so a legacy-filled table merges rather than doubling. The full field map is ENRICHER.md § GWAS
effect sizes.

**The class, built in the same item at the lead's call.** The contract test written for the GWAS 410 was run
over every `CLIENTS` row and measured the rest of the class: no client named a 410, and six (`gnomad`,
`eutils`, `cpic` and its `row_count`, `pharmvar`, `currency`) retried every `HTTPStatusError`, asking a 400,
404 or 410 three or four times. Now a retry predicate retries transport, timeout, 5xx and 429 only
(`net.retry_if_transient`), and a 410 raises the client's own `*Retired`, a subclass of its could-not-ask type
(`net.raise_if_retired` builds the one message). Three tests hold it: `test_every_client_names_its_410` (an
equality with the `CLIENTS` labels), `test_a_permanent_4xx_is_asked_once` (400, 404, 410 over every row), and
`test_no_retry_policy_in_the_tier_retries_a_permanent_4xx`, which walks every `@retry` in the package and asks
its predicate directly, so the withholding clients and the builders' download are covered too. Each client's
404 meaning was checked and kept; ENRICHER.md tables it. The handler shapes were enumerated before the
subclasses landed: no `except` in the tier names a sibling narrowing a `*Retired` could fall into
(`RateLimitedError`, `EutilsRateLimitedError`, `GwasNotFound`), and every `*Unavailable` handler catches it, by design. Each guard was broken once to watch it go red: the
410 arm in `gwas`, a widened `pharmvar` predicate, and `litvar`'s 410 arm.

**What the code review changed before the close.** The effect allele is taken from the `snp_effect_allele` entry
naming the queried rsID (a multi-SNP association's first entry is another variant's); `gwas` retries a 5xx and a
429 too, which moved its status translation out of the retried body into `_get`; v2's `-` is an absent `pmid`;
a templated `next` link is stripped like every other link; the CLI prints `unparsed_effects` and `unusable`;
`associations_for` was a test-only wrapper and is gone. Kept as built: a 404 on the search is could-not-ask and
aborts the pass like any outage, and `size=1000` was measured to return all 386 associations, not assumed.

**Bounded on purpose.** The withholding clients (`grch37`, `ensembl`, `clingen_allele`, Crossref,
`EuropePmcClient.fulltext`) raise nothing by contract. A 410 there is withheld like any other failure, and is
not retried. A handler that records a client's could-not-ask type as `unreachable` records a `*Retired`
there too, with the retirement in its reason, since the subclass keeps every handler catching it.

**Residuals** none

## RM338 — which files under `logs/` ship: `*.log` only, a text allowlist, content-checked text, or images too

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-11-04 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (decided 2026-11-03,
`unattended`) · **Owner** compiler (`_collect_logs`); built by the lead · **Motivating case** S125 in
CONSUMER_SUGGESTIONS_HISTORY.md (just-module-creator `F116`, 2026-10-05) · *related* RM337, RM147

**The ask.** The reporter wants a JSON Lines session ledger (search receipts, fetch receipts, decisions)
to travel with a module, and offers, in order: decide on content rather than the name (`.log`, `.txt`
and `.md` decode as UTF-8, `.json` parses, every non-blank `.jsonl` line parses); failing that, the
allowlist `.log .txt .md .json .jsonl`; and images as a question rather than a request (`png`/`jpg` can
be checked by magic bytes as `LOGO_EXTENSIONS` already is; SVG is XML that can carry script).

**Legality.** No schema moves. `manifest.logs` is a list of `FileEntry`, and `artifact_digest` hashes
`manifest.artifact.files` only, so no module's byte or content identity changes. P3 and P8 do not reach
it. What it changes is exposure: a module that already has a stray `notes.md` under `logs/` starts
shipping it at its next recompile, and a published file is permanent. That is why this waited for a
decision instead of being built unasked.

**Decided (the maintainer, 2026-11-03): content-checked text, plus images.** Of four options put to them, they chose
"Text checked + images". Under `logs/`, `.log .txt .md .json .jsonl` ship when the content agrees: text decodes
as UTF-8, `.json` parses, and every non-blank `.jsonl` line parses. `png`/`jpg`/`jpeg` ship when their magic bytes
match, as `LOGO_EXTENSIONS` is checked, and under a size ceiling. **SVG never ships**, since it can carry script.
A file that fails its check stays behind with RM337's warning, naming the reason. Each file that ships and is
not `*.log` is named in the compile output, so an author sees it before publishing. The size ceiling is the
lead's constant to pick. The rejected options: `*.log` only (the reporter's ledger would never reach a published
module, because the registry compiles by discovery); an allowlist by extension alone (a binary named `.json`
ships); and text without images (images were raised as a question, and the maintainer took them in).
Whether a failed check refuses under `strict` was not put to the maintainer. The default is a warning in both
modes, since this changes no verdict. RM147's advice against a `logs/` *writer* still stands
and is not reopened: this carries the consumer's own ledger, it does not give the format a ledger
schema.

**The split (the lead, 2026-11-04).** RM337 became a minor the same day, because its warning needs a new
`VALID_WARNING_CODES` member. So this patch ships only what needs no new code: the content checks, and each
newly shipped file that is not `*.log` named by a standard-library `logging` line and listed in
`manifest.logs`. The warning for a file left behind, the failed check's reason included, goes with RM337 in
its minor. Until then a file that fails its check stays behind exactly as before, with nothing said.

**What shipped.** `_collect_logs` walks everything under `logs/` and asks `_log_content_agrees` of each file
whose lowercase extension is in `LOG_TEXT_EXTENSIONS` (`log txt md json jsonl`) or `LOG_IMAGE_MAGIC` (`png
jpg jpeg`). Text must decode as UTF-8, a byte-order mark allowed (a Windows editor writes one, and
`json.loads` refuses it); `.json` must parse as one document, and every non-blank `.jsonl` line on its own,
a line being what ends at `\n` (`str.splitlines()` also breaks at U+2028, which JSON allows raw inside a
string). A `.json` nested past the recursion limit raises `RecursionError` rather than `ValueError`; it is
caught too, so the file stays behind instead of failing the compile. An image must be at most
`LOG_IMAGE_MAX_BYTES` (5 MiB, read from `stat` before any byte) and begin with its format's magic:
`\x89PNG\r\n\x1a\n` for png, `\xff\xd8\xff` for jpg and jpeg, so a JPEG named `.png` stays behind. Each file
that ships this way is named by an info line on `just_dna_compiler.compiler` (*"logs/notes.md ships with the
module (its content matches its name)"*) and, because the CLI configures no logging and an info line is
therefore invisible there, by a `log ships: logs/notes.md` line in `just-dna-compiler compile`. Five choices
the decision did not settle:

- **`*.log` is not checked.** A `.log` under `logs/` ships whatever its bytes, as before. Checking it would
  silently drop a `.log` with one latin-1 byte that shipped at the previous compile, and RM337's warning,
  the only thing that could say so, has not landed. Only an exact lowercase `.log` takes this path; a
  `.LOG` is checked as text.
- **The ceiling is 5 MiB.** That is the line this repository already draws for anything that travels (a
  larger asset goes through Git LFS), and it sits far above a figure or a screenshot. An image above it is
  not a log.
- **Hidden paths and symlinks do not take the new route.** A path with any part starting with `.` under
  `logs/` is tool state (an editor's checkpoint, an agent's `settings.local.json`), and a symlink can reach
  outside the module; either would ship a valid file nobody put there to publish, and a published file is
  permanent. Both stay behind as they did before. A hidden or linked `*.log` still ships, as it always did.
- **The top level is unchanged.** Beside the spec only `*.log` is discovered; the decision is about
  `logs/`. An explicit `log_files` list still ships whatever it names, checks or not.
- **Text has no size ceiling**, as `*.log` never had one; the decision asked for one on images only.

`LOGO_EXTENSIONS` turned out to be checked by extension only, not by magic bytes, so there was nothing to
reuse: the magic table is new, and the logo is left as it was.

Tests: `compiler/tests/test_logs.py`. One module carries fourteen files that ship (three `.log`: one with a
latin-1 byte, one under a hidden directory; a `.jsonl` with a blank line, one with a raw U+2028 in a string,
and one with a byte-order mark; `.json`, and one with a byte-order mark; `.md`; `.txt`; png, jpg and jpeg
with real magic; an upper-case `.JSON`) and a png exactly at the ceiling, beside sixteen that stay behind
(malformed `.json`, a `.jsonl` with one bad line, a GIF named `.png`, a PNG named `.jpg`, an SVG, latin-1
`.txt`/`.md`/`.json`, a `.json` nested past the recursion limit, a `.bin`, a `.zip`, three valid files on
hidden paths, a symlink to valid JSON outside the module, and a real png one byte over the ceiling). It
asserts the exact set in `manifest.logs` and in the output's `logs/`, the info line for each newly shipped
file and for nothing else, warnings and `warnings_summary` identical to a compile with `authoring.log`
alone, and both identities unchanged. `compiler/tests/test_cli.py` asserts the `log ships:` lines, which
failed before the CLI printed them. Each of fifteen mutations (no magic test, no size test, `>=` at the
ceiling, the first `.jsonl` line only, `.json` not parsed, latin-1 instead of UTF-8, the byte-order mark
kept, `splitlines()` for `.jsonl`, `RecursionError` uncaught, a case-sensitive extension, no info line,
`.log` checked, SVG admitted, hidden paths admitted, symlinks admitted) turned a test red before the code
was kept.

**Residuals** RM337 — the warning naming each file left behind under `logs/`, the failed check's reason
included; the logo stays extension-checked and is not reopened here

## RM340 — the VRS-coverage warning counts alleles with no ALT and does not point at the record that says why

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-11-04 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (message text) · **Owner**
compiler (`_vrs_coverage` warning) ·
**Motivating case** S127 in CONSUMER_SUGGESTIONS_HISTORY.md (just-module-creator `F118`, 2026-10-25) ·
*related* RM251, `@unreachable-not-absent`, `@answered-is-not-absent`

**What stands of the report.** After RM251, `source="authored"` rows with empty `ref`/`alts` are two
populations: rows with no rsID, which no refresh can fill, and rows whose live rsID the injected Ensembl
snapshot predates, which a newer snapshot would fill. The reporter's correction found the split already
stated, by name, in `verification.json`'s `rsid_coordinate_agreement` record (*"absent from this
snapshot is not absent from Ensembl"*). The rows are truthful; what is missing is the join. The compile
warning (*"VRS allele identity covers 166/183 … 17 allele(s): no ALT recorded"*) gives no pointer to the
record that explains the gap.

**The patch.** When the spec directory's `verification.json` carries an `rsid_coordinate_agreement`
record with pairs not compared, the no-ALT line of `vrs_coverage_incomplete` says so and names the
record. The compiler already reads the block at compile (`_read_verification_block`). Message text only,
under `@warning-text-is-api`: the existing phrase stays and the pointer is appended. Run
`schema/tests/test_feature_corpus.py`, since `features/` quotes emission text.

**Not taken.** A new `status` member such as `position_only`, or a second `source` value. The reporter
argues against the second themselves, and `@answered-is-not-absent` is the house answer to the first:
`VALID_RESOLUTION_STATUS` is a wire vocabulary every reader of a published `resolution.csv` shares, and
the row was never the untruth. Only the reason it gives is missing, and the reason already exists in the
attestation.

**Residuals** none

**What shipped.** `_vrs_coverage_warnings` takes `unplaced_recorded` and appends a pointer to the no-ALT
reason line alone, after its unchanged phrase. Both call sites (`validate_spec`'s pre-flight and
`compile_module`) pass `_snapshot_unplaced_rsids_recorded(spec_dir)`, which reads the block through
`_read_verification_block`, so an attestation these bytes no longer match points at nothing. The record
is recognised by `compiler.SNAPSHOT_UNPLACED_PHRASE` (*"absent from this snapshot is not absent from
Ensembl"*), which `just_dna_enricher.enrich` now imports to write that same sentence, so the writer and
the reader share one constant. The two sides produce the same line, and the existing message dedup
collapses it to one. No code and no vocabulary member was added.

Tests: `test_fact_tables.py` (the pointer changes exactly one line, the no-ALT one, and that line still
begins with its old text) and `test_verification_block.py` (`apoe_epsilon` carries two no-ALT alleles:
an attested record with the phrase adds the pointer on both sides, once in the manifest; a record
without it, or a stale one, leaves the line bare). `features/compiler/identity_and_vrs.feature` has the
scenario; COMPILER.md's warning catalogue states the pointer.

## RM339 — an interrupted snapshot pull leaves a cache that reads as complete, so it is never finished

**Severity** high · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-11-04 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (enricher only) · **Owner**
enricher (`download._provision_snapshot`, the parquet resolvers, `caches.prepare_lane`) ·
**Motivating case** S126 in CONSUMER_SUGGESTIONS_HISTORY.md (just-dna-registry `warm-caches`,
2026-10-08) · *related* `@a-derived-lane-has-parents-and-an-absent-parent-is-not-an-empty-result`,
`@a-failed-fetch-is-not-a-no-op`

**Reproduced 2026-11-03.** A cache directory holding one footer-valid `homo_sapiens-chr1.parquet` and
nothing else: `ensure_snapshot` returns it without touching the network. `if existing and not corrupt:
return cache_dir` trusts any non-empty set of whole files, and the `.part`-then-rename staging that
keeps each file whole is exactly what makes an interrupted pull look finished: every file present
verifies, and the missing ones leave no trace. The lane's `resolve()` inherits the answer, so
`warm-caches`, its dry run and just-dna-lite's `prepare-caches` agree the lane is present. In the
reported run that was 3 of 25 chromosomes, and `enrich` would have resolved rsIDs against them silently.
Every snapshot sharing the helper has it.

**The patch.** Trust a cache only when it carries a record of a finished pull and every file the record
names is present and whole; without one, fetch what is missing and skip what verifies, which keeps "no
network on a warm cache". The reporter's candidate writes that record at the end of a successful pull.
`release.json` is already fetched last, after every parquet, so where a repo publishes one its presence
marks a finished pull; whether it lists the files, and whether every lane's repo publishes one, is the
first thing to check when building, before adding a file to the layout (`locations`, and
`docs/CACHE_SURFACE.md`'s checklist). Caches provisioned before the record existed either refetch once
or are compared with the remote listing the first time the network is reachable; that choice is the
build's. Second, smaller: name `HF_HUB_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` in the error a read timeout raises, since the
10 s default is short for files of 0.5–1 GB.

**Residuals** none

**What shipped.** `release.json` could not be the record: it lists no files, and the Ensembl lane, the
reported one, publishes none. The record is a new file, `locations.PULL_RECORD_FILENAME`
(`pull-record.json` beside `data/`), kept out of `SNAPSHOT_ROOT_FILENAMES` so no publish carries it.
`_provision_snapshot` lists the data and the sidecar directories, writes the record atomically, and only
then downloads. **Written first rather than last**, because a record written at the end leaves an
interrupted pull looking exactly like a cache from before the record existed.

- `locations.snapshot_record_missing` answers three ways: `[]` (complete), the named files that are absent
  or fail the footer check (an unfinished pull), or `None` (no record). Both parquet resolvers return
  `None` for an unfinished pull, so `cache status`, `prepare`, `warm-caches` and `enrich` stop calling
  it present; Ensembl's prebuilt `.duckdb` keeps its standing. The footer check moved to
  `locations.parquet_footer_ok`, kept importable as `download._parquet_footer_ok`.
- A recorded complete cache is not even listed. A cache with no record (built here, or pulled before
  RM339) is compared with the listing once, fetches what it lacks and gains a record. When the listing
  cannot be read it is used as it is, with a warning that its completeness is unknown, and no record is
  written.
- `prepare_lane` sends an unrecorded parquet cache in the default directory through `ensure` once, when
  the terms permit a pull, and reports `pulled` if files arrived. An override pointing elsewhere, a
  gated lane under an unstated use, and a recorded cache stay `present` as before.
- A read timeout (`httpx.TimeoutException`, after the transport's retries) raises the lane's own error
  naming `HF_HUB_DOWNLOAD_TIMEOUT` and its current value, and leaves no `.part` behind.

Tests: `test_download.py` (an interrupted pull, run through a fake that lets one download through and
kills the next, is not resolvable and the next call fetches only the two missing files; a truncated
recorded file; a recorded cache asks nothing; an unrecorded one is listed once, completed when partial,
and served offline; the timeout message) and `test_cache_lanes.py` (the `prepare` route, and the three
places it stays `present`). The resolver half was shown on `main` first: a cache holding one of a
snapshot's files resolved as present. ENRICHER.md's `cache pull` paragraph, the `cache pull` docstring
and AGENT_NOTES `@a-failed-fetch-is-not-a-no-op` say the new rule.


## RM343 — duckdb 2.0 spells the hash join `Hash Join`, so a query-shape test goes red on a fresh install

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-11-04 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (a test's assertion; no
package change) · **Owner** enricher (tests) · **Motivating case** the liaison's run of the enricher suite
under duckdb 2.0.0, `docs/UPSTREAM_DUCKDB.md` (2026-11-03)

**Measured.** Under duckdb 2.0.0 the enricher suite gives 2280 passed and 1 failed:
`test_query_shapes.py` asserts `"HASH_JOIN"` in the `EXPLAIN` text, and 2.0 prints `Hash Join`. The plan is the
same hash join, and the timing test passes. `duckdb>=1.1.0` is uncapped, so a fresh install takes 2.0.

**The patch.** The assertion reads the operator name in either spelling. No cap, since nothing else in the suite
moved. Capping a runtime dependency to keep one test's string would hold every consumer back for a test.

**Residuals** none

The liaison's ledger (`docs/UPSTREAM_DUCKDB.md`) keeps the rest of 2.0's read.

**What shipped.** `test_lookup_clin_sig_is_a_hash_join_not_an_or_chain` upper-cases the plan text and turns
spaces into underscores before looking for `HASH_JOIN`. The old assertion was run under
`uv run --isolated --with duckdb==2.0.0` and failed on a plan whose operator box reads `Hash Join`. The new
one passes under the locked 1.x and under 2.0.0.

## RM341 — polars 2.x writes its version into every parquet footer, so one `compiler_version` mints a digest per polars release

**Severity** high · **Status** ✖ **CLOSED 2026-11-04 — the cap was reverted before it was pushed; no cap, the
maintainer's decision** · **Owner** compiler (packaging) · **Motivating case** the liaison's measurement, `docs/UPSTREAM_POLARS.md`
(2026-11-03) · *related* RM342, RM304

**Measured.** `polars>=1.42.0` has no upper bound. polars 2.0 writes `created_by = 'Polars (python) version
<v> (build <hash>)'` into the parquet footer (pola-rs/polars#29106, following the parquet spec). The liaison
compiled three reference examples twice under 1.44.2 and once under 2.1.0. The tables, schema, codec and row
groups are equal, but every parquet's sha256 and every `artifact.digest` differ, while 1.44.2 reproduces itself
byte for byte. P4 pins reproducibility to `compiler_version`, so one compiler release installed beside two polars
releases would mint two digests for one spec, with nothing in the manifest saying why.

**The patch.** Cap `polars<2` in the compiler, which the enricher inherits, the way RM304's `ga4gh.vrs<2.4`
mitigation was shipped. Add a test that reads the footer of every parquet a real compile writes and fails when
the installed polars version appears there, so the cap cannot be lifted quietly. It is lifted only by RM342.

**Residuals** RM342 records the toolchain, so a digest that differs between installs can say why.

**Reverted, and the rule that replaced it (the maintainer, 2026-11-04).** No cap on polars or duckdb. polars-bio
already caps just-dna-lite at `polars<2`, and a second cap here would block every other consumer. The rule:
**the liaison decides adoption blockers and hands the lead an adoption map. A pin goes in only when a new major
is proven to break something, and stays until support is integrated.** When the liaison is unavailable to settle
compatibility and work has to move, the lead may pin as a safety. polars 2.x breaks nothing here: under 2.x the
tables and `content_signature` are equal, and the digest moving between installs is what P4 already scopes to a
fixed toolchain. The cap and its footer test were removed in the commit after the one that added them, both
unpushed. The footer test was dropped as well, because it would go red the day `uv.lock` moves to polars 2.
That move is the liaison's adoption map, item 4: every digest moves once, and the release records that the
content is unchanged.

**What was built, then reverted.** `compiler/pyproject.toml` pinned `polars>=1.42.0,<2`, and `uv lock` changed only the specifier.
`compiler/tests/test_parquet_names_no_toolchain.py` compiles `apoe_epsilon` and reads each parquet's thrift footer
straight from the bytes (the compiler tier has no pyarrow). It fails when `pl.__version__` appears there. Run
before the cap under `uv run --isolated --with polars==2.1.0`, it failed on `diplotypes.parquet` and
`haplotypes.parquet`, naming 2.1.0. Under the locked 1.44.2 it passes. That run checks the liaison's measurement
on this machine rather than relaying it.

## RM320 — PubMind's terms are answered: the ANNOVAR table is CC BY-NC-ND 4.0, so a module carrying it is non-commercial and the build gates on `--use`

**Severity** medium (it moves a compile outcome) · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-10-02 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (a corrected terms constant and the gate it feeds; no schema change) · **Owner** enricher (`licensing.py`, `pubmind_build.py`, `pubmind_draft.py`, `caches.py`, `cli.py`) · **Motivating case** [WGLab/PubMind#5](https://github.com/WGLab/PubMind/issues/5), asked 2026-09-27 and answered 2026-09-28 · *related* RM134, RM289, RM27, S99, `@no-named-licence`, `@acquisition-gate-is-not-a-read-gate`

**Residuals** none

RM134 shipped with `PUBMIND_TERMS` at `None` on every axis because no page stated terms for the
ANNOVAR-distributed table, and named asking WGLab and CHOP as the only unblock. The postmortem listed
it as never asked (P16); it was asked on 2026-09-27. A WGLab collaborator replied that the *lightweight*
PubMind-DB release (aggregated pathogenicity and confidence, via ANNOVAR and Zenodo) is **CC BY-NC-ND
4.0**. The software and the full PubMind-DB stay under CHOP's `LICENSE.md`, and the Zenodo CC BY 4.0
label was their mistake, now corrected. The reply covers exactly the file `pubmind build` reads.

1. **`PUBMIND_TERMS`** is `license="CC-BY-NC-ND-4.0"`, `commercial_use=False`, `share_alike=False`,
   `redistribution=True`, the reading `ARTICLE_TERMS_BY_LICENSE` already gives the licence, and a test
   holds the two equal. `license_url` is the written answer. **NoDerivatives has no axis**, so it is in
   `notice`.
2. **The compile outcome moves.** A `pubmind` licence row now taints, so a module carrying one compiles
   only under `non_commercial`. Before, it compiled under any declaration and the manifest named
   `pubmind` in `unknown_terms_sources`. A module drafted before this keeps its all-null row, because
   `sources.csv` merges never clobber; deleting the row and re-drafting records the terms. That is
   declared here and in the CHANGELOG rather than repaired, because overwriting a recorded licence row
   is the thing the never-clobber rule protects a curator's hand-edit from.
3. **`pubmind build` gains `--use`, and `cache rebuild` gates the lane.** The flag was refused while the
   gate could only skip; with a no-sale source it answers per declaration, as on `clinpgx build`. The
   lane's `terms` field now carries `PUBMIND_TERMS`.
4. **The drafter is still not gated**, on the same rule as before: reading an operator-built snapshot is
   not a fetch. Its warning now names the licence and the `--use non-commercial` the compile will ask for.
5. **`pubmind publish` still refuses**, for a new reason: the snapshot decomposes and normalizes the
   table, which makes it adapted material, and NoDerivatives bars sharing that. The refusal, the lane's
   `unpublished` reason and `release.json`'s `notice` say so.

## RM316 — the `annotated_alt` element rule counts by ALT position, and VCF 4.5's local-allele fields order their values through `LAA`

**Severity** low (medium for the first module that points at an `A`/`R`/`G` FORMAT field with it) · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-30 on `main`, uncut — a patch** · **Owner** format (`vocab.ELEMENT_RULE_MEANINGS`) + docs (the consumer contract) · **Motivating case** [VCF_4_5_AUDIT § 5](probes/VCF_4_5_AUDIT.md), 2026-09-30 · *related* RM53, RM54, RM57, RM313

**Residuals** none

**What 4.5 added.** §1.6.2: `LAA` lists, per sample, which ALT alleles are in play and in what order.
Every `A`/`R`/`G` FORMAT field has a local equivalent (`LAD`, `LPL`, …) read through it, and a file may
carry only the local one. In the spec's example, ALT `A,C,T,<*>` with `LAA=2,4` gives `LAD=20,30,10` as
REF, C, `<*>`.

**What we say.** `annotated_alt` is *"at its index in the record's ALT list, which is element index+1
on a Number=R field"*. On `LAD`, ALT `C` (index 2) is element 1. A module rightly writes
`source_field=FORMAT/AD`. A consumer whose merged 4.5 file carries only `LAD`, and falls back to it
under our sentence, reads the wrong allele's depth: well-formed and wrong.

**The patch (text).** In `annotated_alt`'s meaning and in the consumer contract: resolve a local-allele
field to its global equivalent through `LAA` before applying any element rule, as §1.6.2 recommends.
The value-ranging rules survive unchanged. A `local_annotated_alt` rule is refused, because it would
make the module describe how the consumer's file was merged (P2).

**What shipped (text only).** `ELEMENT_RULE_MEANINGS["annotated_alt"]`, which the authoring reference prints, now says a VCF 4.5 local-allele field (`Number` `LA`/`LR`/`LG`) orders its values by the sample's `LAA` and is resolved to its global equivalent through `LAA` before this or any rule applies. SCHEMAS.md's element-rule contract gains the paragraph with §1.6.2's worked example, and records that a `local_annotated_alt` rule is refused (P2). No rule added, no code. RM315 transcribed the `L*` keys and their `Number` codes in the same batch.

## RM315 — the VCF reserved-key tables we transcribe miss keys the spec reserves, among them `RUC`, and name no spec version

**Severity** medium · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-30 on `main`, uncut — a patch** · **Owner** format (`vocab.VCF_FIELD_NUMBER`, `VCF_COLLIDING_KEYS`, `VCF_NUMBER_MEANINGS`) + docs · **Motivating case** [VCF_4_5_AUDIT §§ 3–4](probes/VCF_4_5_AUDIT.md), 2026-09-30 · *related* RM53, RM54, RM57, RM313

**Residuals** none

**What is missing.** `VCF_FIELD_NUMBER` claims to transcribe the spec's reserved keys, but it lacks
§3's INFO keys (`RUC`, `RN`, `RUS`, `RUL`, `RB`, `RUB`, `CIRUC`, `CIRB`, `SVLEN`, `CIPOS`, `CIEND`,
`CILEN`, `CICN`, …), §4's FORMAT `CICN`, `NQ`, `HAP` and `AHAP`, Table 2's `PP`, and every 4.5 key
(`LEN`, `LAA`, `LA`, the local-allele family, the base-modification aliases). `CICN` is reserved in both
namespaces with different cardinality, like `CN`, and is absent from `VCF_COLLIDING_KEYS`. And no doc a
consumer reads says which spec version the tables describe.

**Why it bites.** `binning._VCF_MEASURE_FIELDS` names `RUC` as the field a `repeat_count` is read
from, and `RUC` is `Number=.`. Probed on `htt_repeat_expansion` with `source_element` emptied:
`INFO/RUC` gives no warning, while `FORMAT/AD` gives `vcf_pointer_unselected_element`.

**The patch.** Transcribe the missing keys, add `CICN` with its sentence in `VCF_COLLISION_REASONS`
(asserted total), and fix the comment placing the structural keys in §5.6 (they are §3 and §4). Add
`VCF_NUMBER_MEANINGS` entries for `LA`/`LR`/`LG`/`M`: it is read through `.get(..., default)`, so a
missing meaning prints the default silently (`@lookup-with-a-default-hides-a-new-member`). Assert
equality between the codes the table uses and the codes the meanings cover. State "VCF 4.5; a key added
after it is unknown and withholds" in SCHEMAS.md and COMPILER.md. Leave the pinned `"is not a whole
number in VCF 4.4"` phrase alone: it is API and still true. The `M[0-9]+[ACGTUN]` family is a pattern,
so its named aliases go in, and the ChEBI-numbered form stays unknown. No new code.

**What shipped.** `VCF_FIELD_NUMBER` now holds every key VCF 4.5 reserves: Table 1, Table 2 (with `PP`, `LEN`, `LA`, `LAA`, the local-allele fields and the ten named base-modification aliases in their `M`/`DPM`/`ADM` forms), and the keys §3 and §4 reserve (the structural, copy-number and tandem-repeat keys, `RUC` among them). It was extracted from the 4.5 LaTeX and compared back to it: nothing missing, no `Number` disagreeing. The extractor's header regex also picked up example-only keys (`ALLELEID`, `ASP`, `RSPOS`, `dbSNPBuildID`), which were left out because the spec does not reserve them. `CICN` joins `VCF_COLLIDING_KEYS` with its reason. `VCF_NUMBER_MEANINGS` gains `LA`/`LR`/`LG`/`M`. Three tests: the multi-valued codes the table uses equal the codes with a meaning; every key reserved in both namespaces is a named collision (a subset, because `AF` is a collision by practice); and the audit's probe, `INFO/RUC` with no element rule, now draws `vcf_pointer_unselected_element`. All three fail on the old table. The comments and SCHEMAS.md/COMPILER.md state VCF 4.5; the pinned `is not a whole number in VCF 4.4` phrase is untouched. No new code: an existing warning fires on more pointers, and an existing collision set gains a member.

## RM314 — the reference-block rule we print reads INFO `END`, which VCF 4.5 made a cross-sample maximum, so a multi-sample file credits one sample's block to another's positions

**Severity** medium · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-30 on `main`, uncut — a patch** · **Owner** format (the `callable_from` description) + docs (SCHEMAS.md, the consumer contract) · **Motivating case** [VCF_4_5_AUDIT § 1](probes/VCF_4_5_AUDIT.md), 2026-09-30 · *related* RM53, RM54, RM57, RM313

**Residuals** none

**What 4.5 changed.** §5.5 moves a gVCF reference block's extent to a per-sample FORMAT `LEN`. §1.6.1
deprecates INFO `END` and, when it is present, makes it *"the maximum end reference position"* over
every sample's `LEN`. §5.5 also says a position covered by a sample's own earlier `<*>` block carries
`GT=.` for that sample.

**What we tell consumers.** `VariantRow.callable_from`'s description and SCHEMAS.md's *Reference
evidence is a block* paragraph say a block is *"one record with END="*, found by interval containment
on it. In the record `1 100 . A <*> . . END=199 GT:MIN_DP:LEN 0/0:30:100 0/0:30:10`, sample two called
100–109 only, and our rule credits it with 150. For a `requires_callable` row at 150 that is a
confident absence nobody screened for: the direction SCHEMAS.md itself calls dangerous. The `GT=.` rule
errs the safe way, but our text still sends the consumer to the wrong record.

**The patch (text only).** Read the sample's own FORMAT `LEN` first, and `END` only where `LEN` is
absent (the spec's own fallback). A `.` GT inside that sample's own earlier block is that block's call,
not a no-call. Update the `callable_from` description, the SCHEMAS.md paragraph and its quoted 4.4
record, and the consumer contract. No column, no validator: P3 and P8 are not reached. Severity is
stated for the file the spec permits; no real multi-sample 4.5 file with per-sample `LEN` was measured.

**What shipped (text only).** `VariantRow.callable_from`'s description and SCHEMAS.md's consumer contract (*Reading the VCF the pointers point at*) now read a block's extent from the sample's own FORMAT `LEN` first and INFO `END` only where `LEN` is absent, say why (4.5 makes `END` a cross-sample maximum) with the audit's two-sample record, and read a `.` GT inside the sample's own earlier block as that block's call. The quoted 4.4 record is gone from the paragraph rather than kept beside a rule it no longer illustrates. No column, no validator, no warning code; nothing pinned the old wording.

## RM310 — `cache rebuild --only cpic` lets a CPIC outage escape as a traceback, and the lanes after it never build

**Severity** medium · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-29 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (one handler, no surface) · **Owner** enricher
(`caches._rebuild_cpic`) · **Motivating case** found 2026-09-29 while vetting RM288 for the 0.8 pt1
proposal · *related* RM288, RM97, RM101, `@client-exception-contract`

**Residuals** RM288 — which side owns a builder's error list, so the next caller cannot name half of it

**Reproduced.** `caches._rebuild_cpic` catches `(cpic_build.CpicBuildError, ImportError, OSError)`.
`cpic_build.build_snapshot` fetches through `CpicClient`, which raises `CpicError` on a transport
failure or a 5xx (RM97 made it do so), and nothing in `cpic_build` translates it. With
`build_snapshot` stubbed to raise `CpicError("… 503")`, `_rebuild_cpic` raises instead of returning a
failed `RebuildOutcome`. The CLI's `cache rebuild` loop (`cli.py`, the `rebuild_lane` call) and
`rebuild_caches` have no per-lane backstop, so every lane after CPIC in registry order is neither
built nor reported. `prepare_caches` survives only through its catch-all `except Exception`, which
reports the lane as a generic crash.

**Why it happened.** It is the list shape RM288 records: the CLI's `cpic_build_` names
`(CpicError, CpicBuildError)` correctly, and the second caller, written later, named one of the two.
That is the drift RM96 was the lesson for, and it is the first incident RM288 had lacked.

**The patch.** Add `cpic.CpicError` to the handler, and a test that stubs each builder's client to
raise its documented type and asserts every `_rebuild_*` returns an outcome rather than raising. The
test walks `CACHE_LANES`, never a hand-kept list. Which mechanism stops the next drift is RM288's
question, not this one's.

**What shipped.** `_rebuild_cpic` names `cpic.CpicError` beside `CpicBuildError`, as the CLI's
`cpic build` does. `test_rebuild_adapters_contain_their_errors.py` walks `CACHE_LANES`, makes each
adapter's first builder call raise its documented type (both of CPIC's), and asserts the adapter
returns `built=False` with the error in its detail. A set-equality guard fails when a lane gains an
adapter with no stated errors. With the handler reverted, only the `CpicError` case fails. Routed by
the maintainer through a peer session; the mechanism stays RM288's.

## RM290 — the "vindicated" reading of an unmatched overlay row exists for one overridable table, and nobody decided the others

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-29 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (a registry field; no
finding moves) · **Owner** schema (`overrides.OverlayTarget.vindication`) + compiler · **Motivating case** S60's
*"what we are keeping regardless of the shape"* and RM117, found unhomed by the 2026-09-27 postmortem
sweep (P15) · *related* S60, S52, RM117, RM137, RM311

**Residuals** RM311 — the `gene_validity.csv` case this entry names is not an absence, and it needs a
value comparison rather than a classification

S60 found that an overlay row which no longer changes anything can mean the source caught up: the
author's judgement was later vindicated and the row can retire. The reply kept it as *"a property of
the design rather than a nice detail"*, since S52 had seen the same shape. RM117 built it for exactly
one table: `VINDICATING_OVERLAY_TABLE = "clin_sig_concordance.csv"`, which the compiler routes away
from the generic *"may be mistyped"* finding.

**Confirmed on 2026-09-27.** `OVERRIDABLE_TABLES` has more members, and every other table's unmatched
row still reads *may be mistyped*. On a table whose values a later source release can change (for
example `gene_validity.csv`, whose classifications drift), that is the wrong thing to tell an author
whose correction the source has since adopted.

**What to decide.** Per table, whether an unmatched update has a vindicated reading, and whether that
reading is the only one (as on the concordance table) or one of two, which would be withheld
(`@two-vocabularies-that-do-not-meet-withhold`). Turning the constant into a per-table field on
`OverlayTarget` is internal. Reporting it reuses the existing warning code, so it is a patch.

**Decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-29: yes, with concordance's shape as the default.** Taken as
the shape of the mechanism rather than a reading for every table, because generalising
vindication-by-absence would tell an author with a mistyped `variant_key` that the authorities now
agree, which is the misleading message RM117 was built to remove, reversed.

**What shipped.** `VINDICATING_OVERLAY_TABLE` became `OverlayTarget.vindication`, a closed
`VINDICATION_READINGS` member (`sole` / `withheld` / `none`) with a mandatory `vindication_reason`
beside it, and `VINDICATING_OVERLAY_TABLES` is derived from the registry. The per-table decision,
checked against each writer rather than assumed:

* `clin_sig_concordance.csv` is **`sole`**. It holds contested subjects only and is rewritten whole
  (`concordance.py`), unchanged from RM117.
* `resolution.csv` is **`withheld`**. A re-derivation replaces a subject's locus group whole (RM115)
  and `locus_index` is a position in it, so the author's corrected locus can return under another index
  while the source agrees with them. The generic finding already names every reading.
* The seven merged tables (`frequencies`, `gene_metrics`, `gene_validity`, `clinical_assertions`,
  `literature`, `gwas_effects`, `expression_effects`) are **`none`**. Each writer merges and never
  clobbers, and each key is the source's stable identity, so a source adopting the author's value
  leaves the row in place and the update keeps matching. An absent row was never written, was
  withdrawn, or is mistyped, and none of those is agreement.

**No finding moves**, so `warnings_summary` on every existing manifest is unchanged, and Principle 3
has no correction to declare. Walked tests pin the set to the concordance record alone, refuse a
reading outside the vocabulary or without a reason, and assert that no other table's unmatched update
is ever called vindicated.

**The entry's premise was partly wrong.** It named `gene_validity.csv` as the table where "may be
mistyped" is the wrong thing to tell an author whose correction the source adopted. But a source
adopting it there does not remove a row: a newer curation joins the currency group, the corrected one
stays (`classify_currency` deletes nothing), and the overlay still matches. So the author is told
nothing at all rather than told the wrong thing. The signal is a value comparison of the overlay
against the group's `CURRENT` row, which is RM311.

## RM307 — the AlphaGenome Atlas client has no pacing gate, and the interval one needs is unmeasured

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-29 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (internal behaviour;
no schema, no parquet) · **Owner** enricher (`atlas_client`) · **Motivating case** RM280's pacing half, split off when RM280
shipped its retry half on 2026-09-28 · *related* RM280, RM192, `@shared-pacing-gate`,
`@retry-attempt-floor`

**Residuals** won't fix — a daily quota, if one exists: finding it means spending it, and a hit would
arrive as `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, which is already `AtlasUnavailable` and retried.

**What is missing.** Most retried clients in the tier wait on a `net.PacingGate` once per attempt
(`cpic` and `ensembl` are the other two that do not). `AtlasClient` does not. RM280 gave it the house retry floor, so
`JUST_DNA_HTTP_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` can now raise its attempts, and those attempts are not paced. The
gate is also what counts `spent` (S95), so an Atlas call is the one upstream attempt a host metering
egress cannot see.

**Why RM280 did not build it.** A gate needs an interval, and nothing settles one.
[ALPHAGENOME_ATLAS.md](probes/ALPHAGENOME_ATLAS.md) records that no quota or rate-limit figure is
published and none was measured. Nothing in this repository calls the client from more than one
thread, but `check_variant_impact(client=...)` takes a host's client, so a host threading its work
shares one client by following the injection API. That is the S15 argument for making a gate
shareable in the first place.

**What to decide.** The interval: measured against the service, or a stated courtesy value with no
upstream figure behind it. And whether `AtlasClient` takes an injected `gate=` like the httpx
clients, so a host running several clients can hand them one. Internal behaviour either way, so a
patch.

**Decided by the maintainer on 2026-09-29: measure it, and if nothing needs pacing, record that.**
Measured with the stub called directly, so no retry could absorb a throttle
([ALPHAGENOME_ATLAS.md § 6.7](probes/ALPHAGENOME_ATLAS.md), program in A.8): 479 sequential calls in
90 s, then 1,493 calls from four threads in 70 s (21/s, about 1,270 a minute), all `OK`. Sixteen threads
got *less* through (16.7/s) and 32 of 1,600 calls hit the 30 s deadline, so concurrency degrades before
any quota answers. No `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED` in about 3,570 calls.

**What shipped.** `ATLAS_REQUEST_INTERVAL = 0.0`, stated as a measurement. `AtlasClient` holds a
`net.PacingGate` (its own, or one injected with `gate=`, also on `connect`) and waits on it once per
attempt inside the retry, so `gate.spent` counts upstream attempts like every other client's (S95). A
host sharing one gate across clients sets whatever interval it wants. The probe's *"API quota and rate
limits. Not measured"* line is struck, and a stale pointer in the same probe (A.8 for the two-package
recipe, which is A.6) is corrected.

## RM279 — nothing checks a `conclusion` against the other cells on its own row, so a swapped pair compiles green

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-28 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (the genotype rule, as an
authoring hint) · **Owner** compiler (`conclusion.py`, `hints._check_conclusions`) · **Motivating case**
consumer-note D14 (the 0.7 idea-book), numbered by the 2026-09-27 postmortem (P7), because an idea-book
bullet is not a home · *related* S68, RM308, RM309

**Residuals** RM308 (the same finding at `validate`/`compile`, which needs a warning code and so a
minor) and RM309 (the second rule, a `state` the conclusion negates, never measured)

**What the reporter measured, and what we reproduced.** 20 hits in 1,418 rows at about 60% precision
by hand. The finds that matter are real curation errors: `coronary` `rs17514846` has its `C/C` and
`A/A` conclusions **swapped**, and `rs11591147` is scored `protective +1.2` on `T/T` under text saying
`GG` is protective. `lint_rows` over twelve real `thrombophilia` rows returned no finding on three
more (`rs1799963 A/A` → *"GA carriers have 6.74x risk"*; `rs2519093 C/T` → *"TT genotype is
associated…"*; `rs1799889 G/G` with `state: risk` under *"…is not increased"*). Both measurements are
recorded in the idea-book and the consumer-note triage section of this file.

**Two candidate rules, neither needing an external source.** A conclusion naming a genotype **built
from alleles at this row's own locus** that is not this row's genotype; and a `state` of
`risk`/`protective` the conclusion's text negates. The locus restriction is what makes the first
tractable (an earlier version flagged *"(TG) levels"*).

**Parked on, and the gate is satisfiable now.** A measured precision for the locus-restricted rule over
the reference examples plus the reporter's corpus. A warning an author reads on every compile at 60%
precision is how the channel stops being read (S68). Anyone can run that measurement today, so the gate is not
circular. Being a warning with no schema member, it is patch-class once built.

*Refuted by the build, 2026-09-28.* A warning at `validate`/`compile` is a schema member: it needs a
key in `VALID_WARNING_CODES`, and a new key is minor-class. Only the hint was patch-class, and the
compile half is RM308.

**What shipped, measured.** The gate was a precision for the locus-restricted rule, and it was run
over 653,706 diploid rows: the six curated v1 ports the reporter measured (1,418 rows, from
`just-dna-lite/data/interim/v1_port_0_5`), `reference_examples/`, and the registry's `cardio`, `cancer`
and `pathogenic` modules. The reporter's reading ("names a genotype that is not this row's") fired
**24** times, about 40% real, because a correct row that also names its neighbour (*"AA is protective,
AC carriers less so"*) matches. Reading it as **names genotypes at this locus and never its own** left
14, and four of those were three shapes of prose that are not a genotype: an allele description after
an rsID (*"rs1042718 (C/A)"*), a haplotype across two sites, and (on the registry modules) the row's
own gene symbol (*"variant in TG"*). Excluding those three left **10 findings, all 10 real by hand**:
`rs17514846`'s swapped pair, five rows carrying a neighbour's sentence (`rs1799963`, `rs1800790`,
`rs17228212`, `rs2519093`, `rs6025`), `rs4977574`, `rs11591147`, and `rs17822931`'s strand-mixed
`G/G` row under `TT` text. Zero on every reference example.

**Where it runs, and why only there.** `hints.inspect_rows`, so `hint variants.csv` and the creator's
`lint_rows` report it as a `warning` on the `conclusion` column, naming the row that carries the
genotype the text names, which is how a swap reads as two findings pointing at each other. It does not
run at `validate` or `compile`. A finding there needs a member of `VALID_WARNING_CODES`, and adding one is
minor-class because a reader pinned to an older `just-dna-format` refuses a manifest carrying it. The
missing-sentinel finding already lives on the authoring surface only, so this is the second such hint,
not a new kind. The rule is its own module (`just_dna_compiler.conclusion`) so RM308 calls it from the
compile path without a cycle through `hints`. Every exclusion has a test that goes red without it,
and the two positive tests go red with the check switched off.

## RM280 — the AlphaGenome Atlas client has no retry layer of its own and no shared pacing gate, which RM192 said was filed

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-28 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (the retry half; the
pacing half is RM307) · **Owner** enricher (`atlas_client`) · **Motivating case** RM192's *"What it
did not do"* paragraph and PROPOSAL_0_7_PT4's *Implementation debt* list. The 2026-09-27 postmortem
sweep (P8) found nothing had been filed · *related* RM192, RM194, RM196, RM307

**Confirmed on 2026-09-27.** RM192's client docstring said it carried no `tenacity` layer over the
vendored `grpc_service_config.json` (`@retry-attempt-floor`) and no shared pacing gate
(`@shared-pacing-gate`), and no ROADMAP file named either. The channel did take upstream's retry
policy from the vendored service config, so the client was not unretried. What was missing was the
house layer every other network client has: a floor an operator can raise, and one gate shared
across concurrent callers.

**What was measured.** grpc 1.83.1 caps service-config retries at five attempts, and upstream's config
already asks for five. So `JUST_DNA_HTTP_RETRY_ATTEMPTS` could not raise the Atlas client's attempts,
and a `tenacity` layer stacked on the channel would have multiplied them (5 × N) rather than set a
floor. A loopback server answering `UNAVAILABLE` saw **five** calls for one stub call under the
vendored options, sixteen seconds of grpc backoff, and **one** under the new ones. `_translate` also
classified `INTERNAL` as `AtlasUnavailable`, whose docstring says *retryable*, and nothing retried it:
upstream's config names `RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED`, `UNAVAILABLE` and `DEADLINE_EXCEEDED` only.

**What shipped: option (b), the maintainer's choice.** grpc's retry is off, and the client retries in
the house layer.

- `atlas_client.channel_options()` is what `connect` opens the channel with: `grpc.enable_retries = 0`,
  and the vendored config with `retryPolicy` removed from every method config. The per-attempt
  `timeout` stays, since it is a deadline.
- `AtlasClient._call` is the one retried method, and all three RPCs go through it. It uses
  `attempt_floor(RETRY_DEFAULT_ATTEMPTS)`, which is upstream's `maxAttempts` (5) read from the vendored
  file. Its wait is `wait_random_exponential` with upstream's `initialBackoff`, `maxBackoff` and
  `backoffMultiplier`, which is the form grpc applies them in. It sets `reraise=True`, so each caller's
  `except grpc.RpcError` still translates after the last attempt. Retry inside, translate outside.
- What it retries is `_retryable`, which asks `_translate` whether the status becomes
  `AtlasUnavailable`. The retry set is derived from the classification rather than restated beside
  it, so `INTERNAL` is retried now, and a code moved between arms moves the retry with it.

**What pins it** (`enricher/tests/test_atlas_client.py`). Every `grpc.StatusCode` except `OK` is walked, and the
expected attempt count is computed from `_translate` at run time: the floor's value for a retryable
status, one for any other. The knob is run at `""`, `0`, `1`, `2` and `8`. It is a floor, so the low
values leave five in place and `8` makes eight. The options test asserts `enable_retries == 0`, no
`retryPolicy`, and the vendored `timeout` kept, and a second test probes `connect` itself for those
options. The policy's stop and wait are compared with the vendored JSON read independently. The
package-wide roster in `test_gated_snapshots.py` now lists `atlas_client.AtlasClient._call`, and its
defaults are `{3, 4, 5}`. `test_retry_is_reachable.py` does not see this client: its walk resolves
only `retry_if_exception_type(httpx.…)`, and `_call` has no `except` for it to check. The import-floor
test admits `tenacity`, a core dependency of the tier, so `[atlas]` is still grpcio + protobuf.

**The pacing half was not built.** A gate needs an interval. The Atlas publishes no rate budget, and
ALPHAGENOME_ATLAS.md records that none was measured. Nothing here calls the client from two threads,
but `check_variant_impact(client=...)` takes a host's client, so "no concurrent caller" is true of
this repository and not of its consumers. RM307 carries it.

**Residuals** RM307

## RM297 — the ClinPGx currency check compares a row against an annotation it never cited

**Severity** medium · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-28 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (a warning; the check withholds rather than blocks) ·
**Owner** enricher (`clinpgx.enrich_clinpgx`) · **Motivating case** S122 in
CONSUMER_SUGGESTIONS_HISTORY.md · *related* RM298 (the minor that settles it), `@existence-not-identity`,
`@the-signal-may-already-be-firing-with-the-wrong-words`, `@warning-code-names-the-finding`,
`@rsid-absent-two-readings`

**Reproduced.** `just-dna-seq/pharmgkb@1.0.0` was drafted from `clinpgx_2025-07-05`. It carries three
`rs116855232 + azathioprine` rows citing annotation `1184514050` at `1A`. ClinPGx withdrew that
annotation before `clinpgx_2026-08-05`. Run against the newer snapshot, `enrich_clinpgx` reports
`module says level 1A, ClinPGx says 3` for all three and `unmatched 0`. The `3` belongs to a different
annotation, `1450934767` (Toxicity, azathioprine;mercaptopurine), which has been in both snapshots.

**The mechanism.** The lookup tries `(annotation_id, genotype)`, then `(rsid, drug, genotype,
category)`, then the bare triple. When the row's `annotation_id` is absent from the snapshot, or the
row has none, the fall-through compares it against whichever ClinPGx annotation shares its category. It
then reports a level difference against a record the row never cited, and under `strict` refuses on
it. The same fall-through can also **agree** silently when the other annotation happens to share the
level.

**Why the check cannot know better, and why that decides the severity.** Nothing marks a row as
ClinPGx-derived. `sources.csv` records ClinPGx per `(source, layer)`, and so does
`record_draft_provenance`. `annotation_id` is source-agnostic by its own field description (*"the
source's own accession"*), and a curator may author a row from an article, CPIC or DPWG with its own
accession or none. So an `annotation_id` the snapshot does not hold has **three** readings:

- ClinPGx withdrew it (the S122 case).
- It is mistyped.
- It was never a ClinPGx accession.

A refusal under the third reading blocks a legitimate row with an error its author cannot clear. A
row with no `annotation_id` has the same problem one step earlier.

**The patch, decided with the maintainer 2026-09-27: warn, never block.**

- A row whose `annotation_id` is set and absent from the snapshot stops the lookup. It becomes its own
  finding, warned in both modes and never raised under `strict`. The finding names all three readings
  and says what the snapshot holds at the triple.
- A row with no `annotation_id` whose level is compared only through the category or triple fall-through
  is still reported, but it no longer refuses under `strict`. The row has not claimed that record.
- An id that is present but lacks that genotype keeps today's fall-through.
- A conflict reached through the row's own `annotation_id` is unchanged. It keeps its text
  byte-for-byte (`@warning-text-is-api`) and still refuses under `strict`.
- A new `ClinPgxResult` field is additive. The new warning code needs its `features/` scenario.
- `verification.json`'s `findings` for `pgx_evidence_level` counts the new finding, so moving rows out
  of `conflicts` does not lower a published number for an unchanged module.
- The patch loosens `strict` for fall-through rows. It must declare that in the CHANGELOG entry.

**What the patch leaves open is RM298's.** Knowing *per row* that a row cites ClinPGx is what would
let a withdrawn annotation block again, and that needs an authored column.

**What shipped.** `enrich_clinpgx` collects every row a cited id cannot settle into a new
`ClinPgxResult.withheld` list of `WithheldLevel`s, each carrying one of two lane-local codes
(`VALID_CLINPGX_WITHHELD_CODES`): `clinpgx_annotation_not_in_snapshot` for a cited id the snapshot
does not hold, and `clinpgx_level_differs_from_uncited_annotation` for a row with no id whose category
or triple match carries another level. The first stops the lookup at the cited id and quotes what the
snapshot holds at the row's category, or else at its triple. Each lands in `warnings` in both modes, and
the `strict` gate reads `conflicts` only. The `pgx_evidence_level` record counts `conflicts + withheld`
as `findings` and names the codes in `detail`, which stays `None` when nothing is withheld, so a run
with nothing withheld writes the record it always wrote. An own-id conflict, and a cited id present
without the row's genotype, are unchanged. The codes are not `VALID_WARNING_CODES` members: that
vocabulary is the compiler's, and the finding reaches a compile as `verification_findings_recorded`,
the shape `civic_refutation`'s two codes set. **One widening beyond the entry's letter**: a cited id
absent from the snapshot with nothing at its triple used to be an `unmatched` miss and is now this
finding, because the id is the claim and the entry makes an absent id its own finding.

**Tests.** `enricher/tests/test_clinpgx.py`: the S122 shape (a cited id derived to be absent from the
slice, at a level its category neighbour does not carry) and a row citing no id both refused under
`strict` on the previous tree and now pass with one `withheld` each. The record still counts the
withheld row as a finding. An own-id conflict keeps its text byte for byte, and the two codes have
pairwise distinct sentences. The `features/` scenario sits beside `@check:pgx_evidence_level`.

**Residuals** RM298

## RM289 — two author-facing sentences state something false: `PgsRow.training_ancestry`'s description, and the licence gate's skip for unknown terms

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-28 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (text only) · **Owner**
format (`pgs.py`) + enricher (`licensing.py`) · **Motivating case** RM163's own finding and the S99
reply, both left as sentences, found by the 2026-09-27 postmortem sweep (P15) · *related* RM163, S99,
RM27, `@field-description-is-a-claim`, `@warning-text-is-api`

**Residuals** won't fix — S99's archived reply still calls RM27's axis undesigned, and answered replies belong to the triage seat

1. **`PgsRow.training_ancestry` said "validated in".** RM163 recorded that *"the name says training,
   the description says 'validated in'"* and changed nothing. The description is published by
   `describe`, `requirements` and `json_schemas()`, so it is a claim every author reads.
2. **The skip sentence for unknown terms read as "not recorded yet".** S99's reply said the gate's
   sentence (*"terms could not be established, so the data is not used … the absence of a finding
   either way"*) reads as *not recorded yet* when for PubMind it is *unsettleable*, and called it a
   patch-level candidate for after 0.7.0.

**What shipped.** No drafter fills `training_ancestry`. The one machine that reads it is RM163's drift
check, which compares it against the PGS Catalog's `dev` **and** `eval` stages
(`pgs.COMPARED_ANCESTRY_STAGES`, the discovery GWAS excluded on purpose). So the description now says
the score was *developed and evaluated in* those superpopulations, naming both Catalog stages and
excluding the discovery GWAS. A dev-only wording would have matched the column's name and contradicted
the check, which accepts an evaluation-only ancestry as agreeing. The module docstring and two code
comments that quoted "validated in" say the same.

`check_declared_use`'s unknown arm keeps its leading phrase and now says that no declared use changes
the outcome, then quotes what *is* established: the terms' own `notice` and `license_url`. Every source
held at `commercial_use=None` today (`clingen_allele_registry`, `gwas_catalog`, `mane`, `pgs_catalog`,
`pubmind`) is a probed absence whose reading is already recorded in `notice`, so the sentence reads as
*unsettleable, and here is why* rather than as a constant left unfilled. Two `licensing.py` comments
calling RM27's redistribution axis *undesigned* now say it shipped record-only.

**Why a patch.** Both are text: no field, no vocabulary member, no digest moves.

**Tests.** `enricher/tests/test_pgs.py::test_training_ancestry_description_names_the_stages_the_check_compares`
ties the description to `COMPARED_ANCESTRY_STAGES` through a stage-to-word map that must cover the
tuple exactly. `enricher/tests/test_pubmind_licensing.py::test_the_unknown_terms_skip_says_why_the_terms_are_unknown`
walks every unknown-terms source in `TERMS_BY_SOURCE` against every `declared_use` member. Both failed
on the previous tree for the stated reason.

## RM301 — constructing an enricher client exported the whole `.env` into the host's environment

**Severity** medium · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-27 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (decided with the
maintainer that day) · **Owner** enricher (`locations`, every credential reader) · **Motivating
case** S124 in CONSUMER_SUGGESTIONS_HISTORY.md, from just-dna-registry on just-module-creator's
behalf · *related* RM102 (reopened by this), RM100, RM176, RM212, `@credential-where-read`

**Residuals** none — the cache resolvers' export is RM102's closed decision, kept on purpose

`EutilsSettings`, `CrossrefClient`, `PmcIdConverterClient` and `PharmVarClient` called `load_env()` in
their constructors, as did `net.retry_attempts`, the `caches` PharmVar guard, `expression._connect`,
`cli._atlas_client_or_none`, `upload`'s three HuggingFace sites and `download`'s two provisioners.
`load_env` is `load_dotenv(override=False)`, so each exported every key in the working directory's
`.env`, not only the credential it read. just-module-creator resolves its settings in layers and tells
an author which layer a value came from. After one of these constructors ran, every file value read as
an exported shell variable.

**What shipped.** `locations.env_value(var)` returns the process environment's value if the variable
is present, else the nearest `.env`'s, and writes nothing. The precedence is `load_env`'s: an exported
value wins and an exported empty string stays empty. Every credential reader above uses it, so RM100's
guarantee (the credential arrives whatever the call order) holds without the export.
`missing_credential_reason` gained a third reading for a key the `.env` sets empty. `net` memoizes the
file's value once and re-reads the environment on every call.

**Why a patch.** The export was a side effect, not a promise. The only code it breaks is host code that
reads a variable which exists only in a `.env`, after constructing one of our clients, and relies on us
to have exported it. That is the call-order dependence RM100 called a bug. RM102's two rejected repairs
stay rejected: no default flips, and nobody's file is filtered.

**Tests.** `enricher/tests/test_env_value_exports_nothing.py` constructs the four clients in a
subprocess whose only source is a `.env`. It asserts that each credential arrived and that none of the
file's keys is in `os.environ`, and it fails on the pre-fix tree with the credentials present and the
whole file exported. An AST walk keeps `load_env()` inside `locations`. `test_dotenv_credentials.py`'s
two before-the-fix probes and RM212's structural check now target `env_value`. The first full run turned
up the fix's own side effect: the HuggingFace sites now consult `env_value("HF_TOKEN")` before
`get_token()`, so the upload tests, which stub `get_token()`, received the real token from this
repository's `.env` instead of the stub's. `HfApi` was mocked, so nothing left the machine. An autouse
fixture in the enricher `conftest.py` now sets `HF_TOKEN` to empty for every test.

## RM299 — `stats.pathogenic_count` says "pathogenic" and counts both pathogenic tiers, per genotype row

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-27 on `main`, uncut — a patch** (field descriptions) ·
**Owner** format (`manifest.Stats`) · **Motivating case** S123 in CONSUMER_SUGGESTIONS_HISTORY.md ·
*related* S43, RM300

**Residuals** RM300

`Stats.pathogenic_count` sums the legacy `pathogenic` boolean over authored `variants.csv` rows. The
boolean folds `likely_pathogenic` into `pathogenic` by design (P8 pins it; SCHEMAS.md has said so
since S43), and a module carries one row per genotype. The field's description said only *"Rows
flagged ClinVar-pathogenic"*. A catalog read `just-dna-seq/pathogenic@2.0.0`'s 617,822 as that many
pathogenic variants: twice the module's 308,990 variants, with about a third of the rows
`likely_pathogenic`. `benign_count` has the same fold and `clinvar_count` the same grain.

**What shipped.** The three descriptions say what they count: authored rows, one per genotype, never
distinct variants. The two tier counts name both tiers their boolean folds and point at `clin_sig`
for the split. The value is unchanged. Redefining it from `clin_sig` would change what an existing
reader is told without any way to know (the S18 precedent), so a per-tier count is additive and is
RM300. `schema/tests/test_manifest.py` pins each description against the derivation: every tier
`derive.*_from_clin_sig` folds must be named in the description of the count that sums that flag.

## RM295 — `cyp2d6_structural` places CYP2D6*4 at a coordinate whose `ref` GRCh38 does not have

**Severity** low · **Status** ✅ **SHIPPED 2026-09-27 on `main`, cut 2026-09-27 as `v0.7.3` — a patch** (a reference-example
correction) · **Owner** docs /
`reference_examples/cyp2d6_structural` · **Motivating case** found by RM291's consumer-join test on
2026-09-27 · *related* RM291

`variants.csv` and `studies.csv` state `22:42127941 C>T` for CYP2D6*4's splice variant. GRCh38 has `G`
there, and Ensembl places `rs3892097` at **`22:42128945`** (`C/A/G/T`), about a kilobase away. The

RM291's test pins the row as its one reference disagreement; correcting the example empties that set.
Check the README's prose and any test that reads the example's coordinates in the same change.

## RM291 — no test does what a consumer does: join a compiled module against an independently normalized VCF
